name: parltrack/parltrack
what_it_holds: Scraper + application ('Parliamentary Tracker') that builds a queryable database of European Parliament dossiers, votes, and MEP activity from EP sources; 639 commits, 74 stars. Page did not expose committed data dumps directly but the project is known to publish periodic JSON/DB dumps via parltrack.org.
why_useful: A second, older/broader EU legislative-tracking tool than HowTheyVote; could be used to pull the legislative history of any EU platform-economy/short-term-rental dossier (gap #12) with dated snapshots (gap #4).

name: c-tonneslan/convene
what_it_holds: Python tool (MIT, 12 commits) that pulls municipal meeting data via the Legistar Web API and Granicus scraping into a normalized OCD-shaped JSON/NDJSON/CSV/iCal output, preconfigured for 24 US cities including Philadelphia, NYC, Chicago, Seattle, San Francisco, Denver, and Boston; outputs meetings, legislation with sponsors, vote records and action histories, with worked JSON examples in the README.
why_useful: Lightweight, easy one-command client to pull council-level ordinance/vote histories for STR-relevant cities (SF OSTR, NYC, Denver, Boston) — a smaller, more approachable alternative to the DataMade/opencivicdata stack for gap #12.
time_coverage: current + historical depending on city's Legistar/Granicus retention
geography: 24 preconfigured US cities (Philadelphia, NYC, Chicago, Seattle, SF, Denver, Boston, others)
size_hint: code + README examples only, no bulk committed data
themes: STR regulation trackers and ordinance datasets: city STR law databases, Legistar/LegiScan clients, EU parliament open data, court records (CourtListener/RECAP) on Airbnb litigation
why_all: Lightweight, easy one-command client to pull council-level ordinance/vote histories for STR-relevant cities (SF OSTR, NYC, Denver, Boston) — a smaller, more approachable alternative to the DataMade/opencivicdata stack for gap #12.

name: freelawproject/recap (recap-chrome)
what_it_holds: Issue tracker for RECAP, a crowdsourced Chrome/Firefox extension (main code in freelawproject/recap-chrome, 550 commits) that captures and re-shares PACER federal court filings for free, feeding into the CourtListener/RECAP archive.
why_useful: Complementary tooling to CourtListener for finding and archiving PACER filings in any active Airbnb federal litigation (e.g. host classification suits, regulatory challenges) without paying PACER fees; same gap targets as CourtListener above.
